policy.identity: Exact complete original2024–25 CCD NCES0803360 / CO-0880. Retain full12-digit NCES IDs and native CO-0880-SSSS. Original CDE organization/district0880 and schoolSSSS are already four-digit strings; exact DDDDSSSS is documented by2025 primary CMAS layout page7. No numeric conversion, zero-padding guesses, suffix/name/address matches or detention aggregate99999999 establish school ownership.
policy.population: Prospective pure lower source profiles require exact operational CCD identity, complete As reported offered flags with a grade3–8 offer, no9–13/AE, high bound01–08 and no uncertain ungraded membership. Original CDE October2024 full PK/half-K/full-K/grades1–12 enrollment must reconcile to PK–12 and contain a positive grade3–8 with explicit-zero grades9–12. Offered and enrolled evidence remain distinct. Charters, school types, income extremes, influence and proficiency never select scope. High, mixed, primary, missing-native and uncertain configurations remain outside.
policy.income: Same-year2024–25 Student October K–12 Free and Reduced Lunch Eligibility by School: each school’s own published three-decimal % Free and Reduced fraction times100, preserving source rounding, reconciled to its own K–12 Count and Free and Reduced Count when unmasked. Own K–12 denominator excludes pre-K and matches native grade enrollment after excluding pre-K. No ratio precision substituted for the published fraction, weighted/funding numerator, other-year backfill or masked eligibility reconstructed.
policy.income_definition: Individual household-income application/alternate income form or categorical/direct-certification eligibility; Healthy School Meals for All supplies no-cost meals regardless of eligibility. Universal meal receipt is not universal economic disadvantage. Native October2024 record uses reported schoolwide eligibility, not the spring assessed-grade subset. Primary current eligibility guidance retains the previous-year eligibility carryover up to30 operating days; exact campus survey coverage and October carryover attribution are not independently certified.
policy.assessment: Original July2025 CDE District and School Achievement Results, CMAS2020 Colorado Academic Standards, SCHOOL and All Grades rows for Mathematics and English Language Arts only. These are directly published whole-school grades3–8 CMAS totals. CSLA/Spanish, CoAlt, SAT/PSAT, high/mixed/primary scope and other-year columns remain separate original evidence. No grade averages, suppressed-component recovery, statewide fits or alternate assessment splice.
policy.denominators: Primary2025 CMAS Summary File Layout v3.2 page3 excludes students without scores from performance-level denominators; page10 calls TotNumScored Number of Valid Scores. Use original exact Number of Valid Scores and Number Met or Exceeded Expectations; ratio100*met/N must reconcile to original one-decimal2025 percentage within0.051. Exact valid scores must be at least16 under the existing conservative Colorado extraction threshold. Total records, no scores, participation and enrollment cannot replace valid scores. Source-level counts are evidence only; no fits/interval endpoints are calculated here.
policy.population_rules: Primary layout group001 excludes report-suppressed registrations and specified other-assessment/duplicate, withdrawn, medical-exemption and part-public/part-home-school invalidations; school-level group001 additionally excludes Expelled=1. Whole-summary valid-score population differs from total registrations, October enrollment and income. Retain low participation/representativeness cautions; native primary population rules do not certify complete admissions/program attribution.
policy.suppression: Original - -, *, N/A, blanks and bounded <16 values remain unavailable. Real zeros remain zeros; do not infer suppressed counts from margins, use totals to recover missing grade components or substitute published rates with reconstructed precision. Published whole-school total is used directly and never requires suppressed grade components to be recovered.
policy.combined: Equal mean of usable original whole-school Math and ELA count ratios, with independent subject valid-score counts retained as components. It is not both-subject proficiency and has no invented paired valid-score count.
policy.attribution: CCD charter/type and original names remain source evidence. No verified admissions, virtual-provider, program or geographic classifications; names and charter status never supply those attributes. Missing Gilliam CO-0880-9803 is not joined to the statewide detention aggregate by name or difference. Exact native school IDs determine attribution.
policy.release: Source/cohort audit only pending independent source review, separate numerical review and later integration. All source/modeling approvals remain false; no model results, canonical writes or publication.

CMAS and CoAlt Summary File Field Definitions – Spring 2025 2 
CO Summary File Field Definitions 
Listed below is the file layout for the CMAS science, social studies, mathematics, and English language arts (including Colorado Spanish language arts) and CoAlt science and social 
studies Summary Data Files and instructions for accessing the files. The district and school files are in .csv format. The first row of the file contains the headers; subsequent rows 
contain the data.  
The Summary Data File (page 6) provides aggregate student performance data for the district or school. The data is aggregated at the district or school level as well as a number of 
demographic group disaggregations. Each level of aggregation is reported on a separate row. The list of reported groups is in the Disaggregated Groups and Descriptions table 
(pages 3-5). 
• O
nly students with scores are included in the aggregated score field calculations.
• Students without scores are not included in the denominator for average scores or the percent of students in a performance le vel.
T
he district files include the district’s schools in addition to the district level data. 
I
n the Summary Data File, Columns A (Level) to AO (Total Number State Use Only 11), contain the same data as the Performance Level Summary Report. The rest of the file has the 
aggregate data reported on the Student Performance Report, District Summary of Schools, Content Standards Roster, and Evidence Statement  Analysis Report (math and ELA/CSLA 
only). The second section of the file is not disaggregated by demographic group. Only the standards appropriate for a particular content  area contain information (e.g., Reading Scale 
Score and Writing Percent Earned are blank for math). 
N
ote: Some fields may be filler in the separate CMAS and CoAlt files. CMAS science and social studies and CoAlt science and social studies fields start on page 11. Math, ELA, and 
CSLA fields start on page 20.  
Ex
porting the Student Data File 
1. Sign into PearsonAccessnext.
2. Select the administration from the administration dropdown in PearsonAccessnext.
3. Select Published Reports under the Reports dropdown menu.
4. Click on the name of the file name to download.
Note: Use the Search field to easily locate the “summary data file” if multiple results are available. 
Importing the file into Excel 
1. Open Excel.
2. Select the Data tab.
3. In the Get External Data group, select From Text.
4. Locate the downloaded Student Data File.
5. Double -click the file name or select the file and click Import.
6. The Text Import Wizard will open.
Step 1: Set original data type to Delimited. Select Next. 
Step 2: Set delimiter to Comma only. Select Next. 
Step 3: To retain leading zeros on fields (e.g., grade), first select all fields in the data preview, then select Text  as the column data format to import data as text. 
Select Finish.

Calculations

Pupil Membership Data Calculations

Each year all public school districts and facilities across the state of Colorado participate in the Student October Count data submission to the Colorado Department of Education (CDE). The purpose of this data collection is to obtain required student level data as provided for by state statute, including information regarding students’ funding eligibility as outlined in the Public School Finance Act of 1994, as amended (22-54-101, C.R.S.). The Colorado Department of Education collects these data through the Data Pipeline system with the Information Management Services (IMS) unit of CDE overseeing the collection.

The Student October Count is based on a one (1) day membership count in which districts are asked to report all students who are actively enrolled and attending classes through their district on that date. While the submission should only include those students who meet the membership and scheduling requirements as of the pupil enrollment count day, the actual submission process begins in September and closes mid-November. Districts should refer to the Student October Count data submission documentation distributed by the IMS unit at CDE for further information regarding the actual submission process and data element definitions.

Definitions

Pupil Membership Data Definitions

Membership

Membership is defined as enrollment and attendance for a student. Students must be enrolled by count date (typically October 1st) or an alternate count date if used. Students must establish attendance prior to count day during the current school year and resume attendance within 30 days following the count day. Students that are counted in membership are indicated with Pupil Attendance Information codes 01-08 to prevent duplicate counts from occurring. Note: Some datasets separate detention center students in a separate category.

Home Based Education

There are two types of home school students: home school students that receive some educational services from a district and home school students that receive no educational services from a district. Home school students participating in district run enrichment programs are tracked, as is any funding associated with their enrollment in an enrichment program. If a home school student is receiving part-time services from multiple districts, the student may only be submitted for a maximum of part-time funding by one district. The other type of home school student is 100% home school. Families will send a form into the district notifying them of the family’s intent to home school. This district reported data is a count of the number of students within a district who are 100% home schooled and not receiving and district lead enrichment by grade level. There is no funding tied to this second group of home school students.

Instructional Program/Service Type (IP/ST)

Services provided by schools and/or districts for students identified as belonging to one or more of the categories below at any point during that school year:

Students with Disabilities

Students who have been formally identified as having physical or health conditions that may have a significant impact on the student’s ability to learn and therefore warrant placing the student on an Individual Educational Program (IEP).

Multilingual Learner (also known as English Learners)

Students who have been identified as Non-English Proficient (NEP), Limited English Proficient (LEP), or Fluent English Proficient Monitor Years 1 and 2 (FEP Monitor 1, FEP Monitor 2). Non-English Proficient is defined as a student who speaks a language other than English and does not comprehend, speak, read, or write English. Limited English Proficient is defined as a student who comprehends, speaks, reads, or writes some English, but whose predominant comprehension or speech is in a language other than English. Fluent English Proficient students in year 1 or 2 of monitor status are students who have spoken, or currently speak, a language other than English, but who can comprehend, speak, read, and write English comparable to their monolingual English-speaking peers. Districts must provide language services to all English Learners.

Economically Disadvantaged (Free/Reduced Lunch)

Student qualifies for either the free or reduced lunch program. 

Migrant

Students enrolled in a specially designed program for children who are, or whose parent or spouse is a migratory agricultural worker, and who, in the preceding 36 months, in order to obtain, or accompany such parent or spouse in order to obtain, temporary or seasonal employment in agricultural work has moved from one school district to another.

Title 1

Students in schools receiving grants under Title I, Part A of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) who are beneficiaries of educational resources paid with those Title I funds. For schools that operate schoolwide (SW) Title I programs, all students are considered Title I and are eligible for support and services. For schools that operate targeted assistance (TA) Title I programs, only students identified as at risk of failing to meet Colorado’s academic achievement standards who receive supports and services paid with Title I funds are considered Title I students. School Title I designation and grant formulas are based on the numbers of students eligible for free or reduced cost meals (FRM).

Homeless

According to the McKinney Act, a “homeless individual” lacks a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.

Gifted and Talented

Students who have been formally identified, using district wide procedures aligned with CDE guidelines, as being endowed with a high degree of exceptionality or potential in mental ability, academics, creativity, or talents (visual, performing, musical arts, or leadership).

Online

Students who have been identified as online students are enrolled in an online school or program. These students are indicated with a Public School Finance Funding Status of 91 Full-Time Online (Single District), 92 Full-Time Online (Multi-District), 94 Part-Time Online (Single District), 95 Part-Time Online (Multi-District) or 96 Not Eligible, Online (Single or Multi-District).

Immigrant

Students are an immigrant if their age is 3 through 21, were not born in any state and have not been attending one or more schools in any one or more states for more than 3 full academic years.

Section 504

Students identified as having a disability under regulations implementing Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 but may or may not be eligible for special education placement under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act.

Q: When is this data posted each year?

Student Data Privacy

Pupil Membership Data Privacy

Data privacy guidelines are applied to publicly reported district and school level pupil membership data to maintain student data privacy. The methods for student data privacy include focused N size suppression and overall total count suppression. While complicated, these methods ensure student data is protected while providing transparent information regarding attendance data as much as possible. Detailed information regarding the data privacy guidelines applied to published data can be requested from the contact at the bottom of the website.

Determine Program Eligibility

School meals are available to every student and help kids stay healthy and ready to learn. Some families may qualify for free or reduced-price meals by completing an application or through direct certification.

School Meal Eligibility

  • School Meal Eligibility Overview
  • Tips for Collecting Family Income Information
  • Student Eligibility Carryover
  • Information Release & Privacy

School Meal Eligibility Overview

Sponsors determine student meal eligibility through household income applications or direct certification. Federal reimbursement is provided for each meal served based on USDA rates for free, reduced-price, or paid meals.

Sponsors in the Healthy School Meals for All Program provide no-cost meals to all students, regardless of eligibility. Even so, it’s important for households to complete income forms so sponsors can maximize federal reimbursement and families can access other benefits, such as reduced school fees.

For the National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program, all disclosure requirements apply when using eligibility information for non-meal purposes. Public school districts must also report free and
reduced-price eligibility totals for the annual At-Risk/Free Lunch October Count.

Eligibility Resources

Eligibility Manual for School Meals

Free and Reduced Price Meals FAQ

Dates & Deadlines webpage

Tips for Collecting Family Income Information

  • Provide consistent and clear communication on how families can apply
  • Promote online application as a component in online school registration
  • Include application and return instructions in Friday folders
  • Mail paper applications with pre-paid return envelopes or designate a drop-off point
  • Hold office hours for application assistance
  • Directly certify students and extend eligibility to household members to the greatest extent possible
  • Use marketing materials to promote applying

Student Eligibility Carryover

A student’s free or reduced-price meal eligibility from the previous school year carries over for up to the first 30 operating days of the new school year, or until a new eligibility determination is made. After the carryover period ends, students will be charged the paid meal rate unless they are directly certified or a new application has been approved.

This file includes background information on the data file release separated into state data notes, metadata provided by states, and post-submission data revisions. The information is provided in separate tabs and described below:

Data Notes (green tab) - this table provides information on data anomalies in the CCD data files. The filters on the column headers can be used to filter the notes to a data file or issue type. Note that the notes tie the comments states provided to specific data errors. Refer to the CCD Business Rules tab for more information on each error. Also note that the error row includes the NCES LEA or school ID for all entities flagged with that error (as appropriate).
CCD Grades Offered Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state on the grades offered within the state beyond the standard grades PK-12 (ungraded, G13, adult education).

CCD Membership Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state the state can differentiate grades offered versus grades enrolled at the district level as well as several fields that provide more information related to prekindergarten and kindergarten enrollment.
CCD Staff FTE Metadata - Indicates whether, according to metadata provided by the state teachers may be assigned to ungraded classes.

CCD Business Rules (yellow tab) - This tab shows the rule logic for all errors references in the State Notes tab. The CCD Business Rules are part of the much broader master EDFacts Business Rules Single Inventory (BRSI). Please refer to the BRSI User Guide for the detailed description of each column. The master EDFacts BRSI provides information on historical changes in busness rules from prior years.
Post-submission data revisions (purple tab) - This tab lists all of the post-submission data revisions/adjustments that were made in the SEA statistical file prior to file release.
Abbreviation Index (orange tab) - This tab provides a description of acronyms used within this document.
Note:  Throughout this document, references to states may include both states and jurisdictions.

The laws governing the California Longitudinal Pupil Data Achievement System (CALPADS) are limited to K-12 students and schools. California preschools are governed differently than K-12 schools and do not fit the model of the California Department of Education’s (CDE) longitudinal data system. While the CDE does collect some data about preschool students, including students receiving special education and related services as required by law, not all preschool programs in the state are statutorily required to report data to the CDE or CALPADS. Only programs with a CDS code and students with a unique student identifier can be reported to CALPADS. This results in an incomplete preschool data set that isn’t representative of the educational landscape in California. Reporting incomplete data sets for public consumption could result in misrepresentation of student groups and diminished reliability of publicly available data provided by the CDE.

The California Department of Education (CDE) Nutrition Services Division collects data on all nutrition programs in the state using unique numerical entity identifiers assigned by the Child Nutrition Information and Payment System (CNIPS). Data are accurate. There are several reasons why this may happen. Direct Certification matches children from a list from ODHS to where the student is listed as enrolling according to the most recent ADM report. The F&R data comes from October meal claims as entered by school districts. If the enrollment boundaries change between the school year, students may have shifted from one school to the next. Districts may have entered meal claim data incorrectly. We do not currently have any system to check these values against when approving claims. Finally, some schools may enter data only for students who ate meals during that month. If a school has a large number of students who are directly certified but choose to not eat meals provided by the school, this contributes to this value as well.

Race data, especially for minority races, can vary from year to year since there is no mandate for reporting the same race every year. The data has been analyzed over the years and LEA reporting of this data for individual students is inconsistent. For example, one year a particular student might be reported as American Indian/Alaskan Native but the following year reported in more than one race (multiracial) category or vice versa. SY2425 race data was compared to SY2324 data for some minority races & this was found to hold true for data reported for SY2425 as well. Also, Vermont’s student population was around 87% white in SY2425 and with minority race populations being small and disaggregated by race and sex, small changes from year to year can result in a change in count of more than 10 and percentage changes greater than 10 percent, the thresholds for this check.

The LEA/SEA AE student counts dropped significantly in SY25 due in large part to fewer students being reported by SU099 Department of Corrections. According to DOC staff, re-organization of the Program Services Division (now known as Risk Intervention Services Division [RIS]) within the Department of Corrections and the subsequent re-alignment of their Student Information Services allowed them to subdivide students into multiple “schools”  for Behavioral Health/Clinical services, Vocational services, Foundational Education, and Community High School of Vermont (CHSVT, an independent school run by DOC) and either aggregate the data or extract distinct data sets for each service. Beginning with SY 2024-2025, they only included individuals actively enrolled in the CHSVT school as of October 1. In the past, they had included all active enrollees without HS diplomas taking Education Foundations remedial reading, writing and mathematics courses as well, but in an October 2025 meeting with VT AOE, all participants concurred that they would only include individuals currently taking high school level academic courses (and exclude those taking vocational training and behavioral health courses).
 
In addition, the number of AE students reported at public schools dropped significantly from 45 in SY24 to 11 in SY25, continuing a declining trend at Vermont public school for at least the past five years. Nine schools that reported AE students in both SY23 & SY24 reported none in SY25. Essex High School (PS388), the school with the most AE students in SY23 & SY24, 17 in SY23 students and 18 in SY24, reported 0 in SY25.

West Virginia has a relatively homogeneous population. As a result, even minor variations that naturally occur within cohort populations may appear as significant differences when disaggregated by individual subgroups.

In recent years, the state has seen an increase in the number of educational programs and circumstances—such as the HOPE Scholarship and homeschooling—that require children not enrolled in public PK–12 schools to obtain a student identification number from the state’s student information system (WVEIS). According to state law, these children are not required to provide any student attribute information (including race/ethnicity) when obtaining an ID number. However, if they later enroll in a public PK–12 school, either full- or part-time, the collection of student attribute data is expected to be completed at the time of enrollment.

Additionally, as users become more proficient with the new student information system, improvements in data accuracy and subgroup classification are ongoing. This increased precision may result in some students—previously categorized in one subgroup—being more accurately reclassified into a different subgroup or multiple subgroups.
